notes: imd/acc on Ethereum mainnet: deploy only the accepted ProjectRegistry, the list of projects whose cashback earns points, decided by IdentityMD oracle panels through Intake v2 (0xa43e...de82), paid in IMD (0xd34a...63b7). Trading cashback is 0.25% to 1% at each project's choice, funded from its existing fees and paid to traders as staked IMD (sIMD); only credits from listed projects earn points. The registry names the live mainnet Stacker 0x0690...f4f0 (launch #1409) in its questions and never calls it; the Stacker is not redeployed. Accepted baseline: Sepolia test run 6 (launch #1463, 0x30a3bb4d75989cb19f83607abc2dffe52a253384), test run 5's registry (launch #1428; live rejection, listing and defended challenge) with one rule text clarified. The eight panel rules are version 3.1 (docs/panel-rules-v2.md): the trader rule rejects the router itself and accepts the address msgSender() reports even when it is a contract; rehearsed with a real panel, 11 of 11 true. A project reporting an owner() may be applied for only by that owner or the project itself; NotProjectOwner otherwise, before any fee. Anyone may apply for a project without an owner. Settings agreed by the owner: challenge bond 20 IMD, challenge cooldown 7 days (604800 s); panel 15 seats with at least 11 agreeing and a 1-day expiry are constants. Each ask pays the oracle fee read live from the Intake via ORACLE_FEE() (0.5 IMD as observed on 2026-10-12). Answers are accepted only from the Intake, for this registry's own open request, once, signed by the oracle signer 0x5598...2982 for this contract and issued after the ask with 300-second tolerance. A yes lists or defends; a no rejects or delists. A defended challenge pays its bond to the beneficiary without restarting cooldown; delisting, failure or expiry returns the bond to the challenger. Refused bond transfers are recorded in bondOwed and claimed with claimBond(to). A beneficiary handoff is allowed at most once per day and never while a question is open. Accepted design limit, agreed by the owner and judged low in launches #1371, #1378, #1428 and #1463: a listed project's beneficiary can challenge its own project and occupy its one-question slot; outsiders revert AskOpen while it is open. Each defended round costs the live oracle fee (observed 0.5 IMD), with the 20 IMD bond paid back to that beneficiary. Each round re-judges the full rules and holds the slot only until resolution or expiry, buys no immunity and does not restart cooldown. Excluding the beneficiary as caller would not close this limit because a second wallet can do the same. Questions are filed under chain 1. No owner; the constructor makes no external call and requires no initialization. Test doubles under test/mocks and test/trial are not deployed.
